bug_semantics: The soffice-backed import/export paths placed working files in the shared directory returned by os.tmpdir() under names derived from non-cryptographic Math.random(), without exclusive creation or no-follow protection. A local user able to predict or race a token could pre-create a symlink at an export source path (or a converter destination path); ExportHandler's fs.writeFile then followed the link and truncated/wrote the linked target with exported HTML, subject to the Etherpad process's filesystem privileges. The import conversion destination was likewise predictable and could receive partially attacker-controlled converted upload content. Shared-host local access and a target writable by Etherpad are required.
flaw_origin: The smallest semantic BIC is eeddf1348f351c92355d010ced56c3b511ca8f46: it created node/ExportHandler.js with Math.floor(Math.random()*new Date().getTime()), /tmp/eplite_export_<token> source/destination paths, fs.writeFile(srcFile, html), and in the same commit registered GET /p/:pad/export/:type in node/server.js. Its direct parent had neither the handler nor route. b13fbbfd73ab18f69d45de382ffb1fc51fe96f1f added the analogous import path two days later. 4fc4a3538148bc995fff989794e91779ed4c847f (export) and b0976a292f70c2c6d344bafd2793aed09027f74b (import) later changed the already-insecure token formula to Math.floor(Math.random()*0xFFFFFFFF); they narrowed/rewrote an existing flaw and are not BICs.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p eeddf1348f351c92355d010ced56c3b511ca8f46 shows author and committer Peter 'Pita' Martischka <petermartischka@googlemail.com> and only the message 'Added support for document export, no link from the pad so far'; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or other AI trailer and no bot identity.
evidence: First-party GHSA-2jwf-f4xq-f24h / CVE-2026-55086 names src/node/handler/{Import,Export}Handler.ts, affected ep_etherpad-lite <=3.0.0, first patched 3.1.0, PR #7784, and commit 8c6104c5d5daf41f0d454acc04d42dffa0e0d996. Reproduce in the assigned full-history clone: (1) git show --format=fuller --patch eeddf1348f351c92355d010ced56c3b511ca8f46 shows new node/ExportHandler.js computing randNum=Math.floor(Math.random()*new Date().getTime()), writing /tmp/eplite_export_<token>.html with fs.writeFile, deriving the converter destination from the same token, and node/server.js registering GET /p/:pad/export/:type. (2) git ls-tree -r 83829759e9ee59beb28730c761d8d6979a95b359 -- node/ExportHandler.js is empty, while git diff --name-status 83829759e9ee59beb28730c761d8d6979a95b359 eeddf1348f351c92355d010ced56c3b511ca8f46 -- node/ExportHandler.js node/server.js reports A node/ExportHandler.js and M node/server.js, directly proving parent absence. (3) git log --all --follow -S'Math.random()*new Date().getTime()' -- src/node/handler/ExportHandler.ts resolves the semantic line to eeddf1348f351c92355d010ced56c3b511ca8f46 and its later rewrite 4fc4a3538148bc995fff989794e91779ed4c847f; git log -L 159,160:src/node/handler/ExportHandler.ts b96e262782e1ed72999c42cb47fb9140e58fe544 follows the surviving random-token/temp-path lines back across renames and refactors. git show b13fbbfd73ab18f69d45de382ffb1fc51fe96f1f -- node/ImportHandler.js shows the analogous import destination introduced on 2011-07-21. (4) git show --patch 8c6104c5d5daf41f0d454acc04d42dffa0e0d996 -- src/node/handler/ImportHandler.ts src/node/handler/ExportHandler.ts shows both Math.random formulas directly replaced by crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex'); its parent is b96e262782e1ed72999c42cb47fb9140e58fe544, where git blame at tag 3.0.0 still shows Math.floor(Math.random() * 0xFFFFFFFF) in both handlers. (5) git tag --contains eeddf1348f351c92355d010ced56c3b511ca8f46 begins with tag 1.0 (package.json version 1.0.0) and includes 3.0.0; git tag --contains 8c6104c5d5daf41f0d454acc04d42dffa0e0d996 begins with 3.1.0. At tags 3.0.0 and 3.1.0, src/package.json reports versions 3.0.0 and 3.1.0 respectively; git blame at 3.1.0 attributes crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex') in both handlers to 8c6104c5d5daf41f0d454acc04d42dffa0e0d996. (6) git cat-file -p eeddf1348f351c92355d010ced56c3b511ca8f46 gives parent 83829759e9ee59beb28730c761d8d6979a95b359, human author/committer Peter 'Pita' Martischka, and no AI attribution trailer.
reasoning: The vulnerability existed when the reachable export feature was first added in 2011: a non-CSPRNG token selected a shared-/tmp pathname and ordinary fs.writeFile followed an attacker-planted symlink. The later switch from Math.random()*time to the advisory's exact 32-bit Math.random()*0xFFFFFFFF expression did not create the security property; its parent was already vulnerable, so selecting the 2011 rewrite or later TypeScript moves would confuse textual provenance with causal origin. The immediate parent of eeddf1348f351c92355d010ced56c3b511ca8f46 lacks both the handler and its route, making eeddf1348f351c92355d010ced56c3b511ca8f46 the smallest real BIC; it is an ordinary one-parent commit, not a squash requiring decomposition. The import path joined the same vulnerable lifecycle in b13fbbfd73ab18f69d45de382ffb1fc51fe96f1f. Commit 8c6104c5d5daf41f0d454acc04d42dffa0e0d996 directly closes the advisory's predictability window in both handlers with 128-bit CSPRNG tokens and first ships in 3.1.0, after the last vulnerable 3.0.0 tag. Although the later fix commit has Claude co-author trailers and the advisory credits Claude, the protocol expressly limits attribution to the BIC commit object. The BIC is human-authored/committed and contains no AI marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
